title: Rare early works by Fernando Botero featured in major Sotheby's New York show
summary: Sotheby’s is holding a selling exhibition dedicated to the artist Fernando Botero this summer, created in partnership with The Fernando Botero Foundation. Focusing on works created during the artist’s foundational New York period, between 1960–1973, the exhibition brings together paintings and sculptures directly from the Botero family and other private collections, many of which are on public view in New York for the very first time. Botero in New York is the first exhibition dedicated to a single artist to be held at Sotheby’s Breuer building, presented at the height of Sotheby’s Summer Season. Visitors will encounter the evolution of Botero’s painting style across these formative years, an important yet rarely explored chapter in his practice. Each of the 25 works from this period mark a distinct moment in the artist’s development, reflecting the period in which Botero was immersed in New York’s creative circles and in direct dialogue with man

title: From a Steel Town in the Urals to a Booth at Seattle Art Fair 2026
summary: A 21-year-old artist from Asha, a small steelmaking town in Russia's Chelyabinsk Region, about 1000 miles east of Moscow, has been selected to exhibit at the 2026 Seattle Art Fair . In a remarkable achievement, eleven of the twelve Russian works chosen for display at TERAVARNA's booth are by Alina Khafizova (Алина Хафизова). Khafizova is an independent artist who began drawing in childhood and developed her artistic practice from an early age. Creativity has long been part of her family background. Her brother, Marsel' Khafizov, is a professional artist and member of the Union of Artists of Russia, while her father also practiced drawing in his youth. title: Jessica Morgan appointed Director of Tate
summary: The Chairman and Trustees of Tate today announced that leading British curator Jessica Morgan (age 57) currently Director of Dia Art Foundation, has been appointed Director of Tate. The appointment was approved by the outgoing Prime Minister, Sir Keir Starmer MP. Morgan will become the tenth Director in Tate’s history, taking up her new role on 1 January 2027. Jessica Morgan has been Director of Dia Art Foundation since 2015. Based in New York, Dia is a multi-sited organisation which commissions and organises artist projects and exhibitions, cares for a growing collection of modern and contemporary art, and stewards several major site-specific art installations across the USA and Germany. Under Morgan’s leadership Dia has become a more expansive and dynamic

title: Restoration of Jacopo Marieschi's 18th-century ceiling painting completed in Venice
summary: The transformational conservation of Jacopo Marieschi’s splendid 18th-century painting Saint John Adoring the Relic of the True Cross from the ceiling of the Church of San Giovanni Evangelista has been completed, thanks the generous support of Arnold M. Bernstein. The painting, created about 1760, is now temporarily displayed in the Atrium of the Scuola Grande di San Giovanni Evangelista through the end of November 2026, allowing visitors the once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to admire it up close before it is reinstalled high on the ceiling of the adjacent church. This intervention represents a rare instance where an 18th-century artwork had never previously undergone a complete restoration. Prior to conservation, it was in a severe

title: The National Gallery brings Mary Magdalene to the nation with new touring exhibition
summary: The first major UK exhibition to explore the legacy of Mary Magdalene through historic and contemporary art is to be staged by the National Gallery at three locations across the north of England in 2027. Partnering with the Walker Art Gallery in Liverpool, the Millennium Gallery in Sheffield and The Auckland Palace in Bishop Auckland, this exhibition will explore the making of Mary Magdalene, looking closely at her legacy shaped by belief, power and misrepresentation. Mary Magdalene: Woman and Myth will bring together eight paintings from the National Gallery’s collection, (works by Carlo Crivelli about 1491-4, Annibale Carracci 1604 and Giovanni Girolamo Savoldo about 1535-40), alongside three loans: Saint Mary Magdalene in the Desert, 1869, by Pierre Puvis de Chavannes (on loan from the Städel Museum), The Tower (Mary Magdalene), 2022, by Jesse Jones, and The Map, 2021, by Alice Maher and Rachel Fallon (both courtesy of the artists). title: Cristea Roberts Gallery presents 'Pop Revisited' exploring 50 years of Pop Art prints
summary: This summer Cristea Roberts Gallery presents Pop Revisited an exhibition of prints and editions spanning a fifty-year period by artists whose practices played a key role in shaping and expanding the visual culture of the Pop-era. Pop Art emerged amidst a proliferation of images in postwar Europe and America. From glossy magazine covers to television advertisements, a new visual language characterised by abundance, aspiration and consumerism captivated a generation of young artists. In 1957, Richard Hamilton described Pop Art as ‘Popular (designed for a mass audience), Transient (short term solution), Expendable (easily forgotten), Low Cost, Mass Produced, Young (aimed at Youth), Witty, Sexy, Gimmicky, Glamorous, Big Business’. More than half a century later, Hamilton’s words remain strikingly relevant. title: Asya Geisberg Gallery announces representation of Orkideh Torabi and Susan Hamburger
summary: Asya Geisberg Gallery announced the representation of Orkideh Torabi and Susan Hamburger. Orkideh Torabi's inaugural exhibition at the gallery, "Kings and Conquerors," was followed by a vibrant booth at NADA New York. Torabi's work was recently included in a two-person booth at The Armory Show with SARAI Gallery in September 2025. In 2021, she had a solo exhibition at the The Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago, IL. Torabi received an MA and BFA from The University of Art, Tehran, Iran, and an MFA from The School of the Art Institute of Chicago, IL, with solo exhibitions at Nino Mier Gallery, Brussels, Belgium; Half Gallery, New York, NY; Western Exhibitions, Chicago, IL; and Richard Heller Gallery, Los Angeles, CA. Her work has been reviewed by The New York Times, AnOther Magazine, Canvas Magazine, The Brooklyn Rail, Gallery Magazine, Elephant Magazine, Los Angeles Times, Hyperallergic, and Juxtapoz. title: Historic McLaren F1 GTR prototype owned by Pink Floyd's Nick Mason set for sale
summary: Estimated in excess of $35 million, chassis 10R is the first McLaren F1 GTR built to the highly developed 1996 specification and one of only two Short-Tail factory “XP” prototypes, alongside chassis 01R, the car that won the 1995 24 Hours of Le Mans outright. Finished in Blood Red with bold yellow “96 GTR” graphics, 10R is the only McLaren F1 GTR to wear this factory-created design. Graphic, unmistakable, and entirely of its era, it remains one of the most recognizable McLarens ever built. Retained by McLaren from new, tested in preparation for the 1996 24 Hours of Le Mans, and later converted for road use by the factory, chassis 10R was acquired directly from McLaren by Pink Floyd drummer and celebrated collector Nick Mason in 1999. title: Amerikahaus Munich presents Jeff Dunas exhibition on American identity and culture
summary: Amerikahaus Munich presents a photographic exhibition by American photographer Jeff Dunas, which focuses on what constitutes the foundation of the United States: its people. Central to the exhibition are his works from the American Pictures series, which were created over several decades. Dunas photographs in cities, small towns, urban peripheries and also rural areas. His motifs are neither iconic nor staged, but rather raw encounters. People in everyday life, in moments of waiting, of pausing, of self-evidence. The photographs appear calm, almost restrained, and that is what gives them their lasting impact. They depict an America characterized by diversity, individual freedom, and social movement. Dunas is not interested in spectacle, but in presence and dignity. His images showcase a country made up of many voices – of different social realities, cultural backgrounds, and ways of life. title: Ferran Barenblit appointed Chief Curator of the 16th Shanghai Biennale
summary: The Power Station of Art announced that, following the careful deliberation of its Fourth Academic Committee, Ferran Barenblit has been appointed Chief Curator of the 16th Shanghai Biennale, which will open in November 2027. Ferran Barenblit is a Barcelona-based curator whose career spans museum leadership and curatorial practice. From 2015 to 2021, he served as Director of MACBA Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona. Previously, he was the founding director of CA2M Centro de Arte Dos de Mayo in Madrid, where he helped shape the institution from its inception, and Director of Centre d'Art Santa Mònica in Barcelona. Throughout his career, his work has consistently engaged with the social, cultural, and historical forces that shape contemporary life. He believes that art is one of the places where societies test their conflicts, desires, imaginaries, and possible futures. title: Apollo Magazine launches 1000-issue online archive
summary: Apollo has launched a complete online archive. Over a century’s worth of issues dating back to 1925 are now available to readers for the first time via Exact Editions. The leading monthly magazine is an authority on art collecting, the international art market, and museum exhibitions - widely considered to be one of the world’s most renowned and respected art publications. The comprehensive, fully-searchable digital resource features all 1200+ issues of the magazine. Readers can see the development of the publication, from its founding by legendary art dealer Joseph Duveen and Finnish art historian Tancred Borenius, to Denys Sutton’s legendary 25-year stint as editor, to the industry-defining present-day art market reporting. title: Fahey/Klein Gallery presents Joel-Peter Witkin career retrospective
summary: Fahey/Klein Gallery is presenting Joel-Peter Witkin: Selected Works 1973 - 2018, an exhibition of photographs by Joel-Peter Witkin spanning more than four decades of the artist’s groundbreaking career. Bringing together seminal works and rare prints, the exhibition offers a timely opportunity to engage with one of the most uncompromising and influential voices in contemporary photography. For over fifty years, Witkin has challenged the conventions of beauty, morality, and representation through meticulously staged tableaux that merge references to religion, mythology, classical painting, and mortality. His photographs occupy a singular space between the sacred and the profane, confronting viewers with images that are at once unsettling and poetic. title: Steve McQueen's End Credits to premiere at The Shed
summary: The Shed will present the New York live premiere of Steve McQueen's End Credits, a special two-performance engagement on September 25 and 26 in The Griffin Theater (545 West 30th Street). Created by the Academy Award–winning filmmaker and artist, End Credits is a haunting confrontation with state surveillance, political persecution, and the enduring legacy of legendary singer, actor, and activist Paul Robeson. For this special presentation at The Shed, McQueen's 72-hour video installation will be transformed into a one-hour, live performance featuring actors Laurel Lefkow, Jeff Mash, Eric Meyers, and Regina Reagan, who recorded the nearly 40 years of surveillance over a 10-year period with McQueen. title: Musée du quai Branly announces 2026 photography award laureates
summary: The winners of the Musée du quai Branly – Jacques Chirac Photography Award are Abhishek Rajaram Khedekar (India) for his project DAPOLI, Lost and Found and Sara Kontar (Syria) for her project On the Edge of Home. The jury also awarded a special mention to Sudanese artist Ammar Yassir for his project I Will Never Find Home. title: Historic Royal Palaces joins Hidden Disabilities Sunflower network to support visitors with invisible disabilities
summary: The independent charity Historic Royal Palaces joins the Hidden Disabilities Sunflower network, marking another step in its ambition to be a charity for everyone and to reduce barriers so more people can experience and enjoy its historic sites. The globally recognised Sunflower symbol helps make the invisible visible, offering a discreet way for people with non-visible disabilities – such as autism, chronic pain, dementia, anxiety or sensory sensitivities – to indicate that they may need additional support, understanding, or time during their visit. By joining the Sunflower network, HRP is strengthening its commitment to creating welcoming, inclusive environments across its palaces. It builds on the charity’s ongoing work

title: FEMSA Collection continues its 50th anniversary celebrations with projects in Mexico and Colombia
summary: As part of its 50th anniversary celebration, the FEMSA Collection presents the next phase of its arts program with projects in Mexico and Colombia, including three exhibitions organized in collaboration with cultural institutions and the commissioning of an artwork in Monterrey. 50th anniversary activities began in March 2026 with “Constellations and Drifts: Latin American Art from the FEMSA Collection,” the most comprehensive presentation of the Collection in Mexico in its nearly five-decade history. The exhibition is currently on view at Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Monterrey (MARCO), where, due to high public demand, it has been extended through August 30, 2026. title: National Portrait Gallery extends its summer hours for Marilyn Monroe: A Portrait
summary: In celebration of Marilyn Monroe’s 100th birthday and in association with the Marilyn Monroe estate, the National Portrait Gallery opened Marilyn Monroe: A Portrait on 4 June 2026. Delving into Monroe’s life, career and legacy, the exhibition explores one of the most famous women of the 20th century through portraits, highlighting the role she played in her own image making, and her inspiration on photographers and artists in her lifetime and long after. Due to popular demand, additional tickets for Marilyn Monroe: A Portrait have now been released, with late-night extensions until 9pm programmed every Thursday in August. August lates are in addition to the NPG’s standard late opening hours on Fridays and Saturdays, providing further opportunities to see the blockbuster exhibition after the Gallery’s daytime crowds. title: New MUMA exhibition explores ancestral cosmologies and speculative fiction
summary: Phantasmagoric performance, speculative storytelling and ancestral cosmologies converge this winter at Monash University Museum of Art | MUMA in Syncretic Wilds, a major exhibition bringing together Gadigal/Sydney-based artist Phasmahammer (the artist name of Justin Talplacido Shoulder) and Minahasan artist Natasha Tontey from 17 July – 19 September 2026. Immersive, cinematic and unapologetically bold, the exhibition stages a charged dialogue between two artists reshaping how history, myth and identity can be imagined from Southeast Asian and Indigenous perspectives. Across performance, film and installation, Phasmahammer and Tontey construct vivid and immersive speculative worlds which are part ritual, part science fiction, challenging dominant narratives and proposing new ways of remembering, sensing and relating.

title: Visa pour l'Image 2026 confronts war, disinformation and the fragile future of photojournalism
summary: Visa pour l’Image will return to Perpignan for its 38th edition with a program that places photojournalism at the center of one of the defining questions of the moment: how can the public recognize truth in an image when artificial intelligence, propaganda and digital manipulation are making that task increasingly difficult Running from August 29 through September 13, 2026, the International Festival of Photojournalism will bring 27 exhibitions, six evening projection programs, professional meetings, portfolio reviews, awards and public discussions to venues across the southern French city. The festival’s professional week will take place from August 31 to September 5, followed by two weeks reserved primarily for school groups. title: Berkshire Museum names new aquarium in recognition of Feigenbaum Foundation grant
summary: Berkshire Museum today announced a grant from the Feigenbaum Foundation in support of its newly expanded aquarium, which will be named the Feigenbaum Aquarium in recognition of the foundation’s longstanding partnership with the museum. The aquarium and museum will open on July 29 following an extensive renovation of the historic institution. Nearly twice the size of its predecessor and relocated to a prominent first-floor space, the Feigenbaum Aquarium will feature terrestrial and aquatic animals, including a Caribbean reef octopus, epaulette sharks, moon jellyfish, tortoises and other species. The expanded space will support live-animal experiences, educational programs and special events exploring biodiversity, ecosystems and environmental stewardship. “The aquarium has been one of the museum’s most beloved

title: Karma opens an exhibition of works by Carole Vanderlinden
summary: Socrates and Phaedrus take a stroll on the outskirts of Athens, their dialogue careening across such subjects as desire, divine madness, the limits and possibilities of language, and the forms reality takes in memory and other representations. Among the claims levied in this text—written by Plato circa 370 BCE and read by artist Carole Vanderlinden nearly two-and-a-half millennia later while she made the oil paintings in Fragmented Thought—is that art cannot be reduced to the elements of its production. Composite parts like materials, techniques, and art-historical conditions cannot account for each work’s singularity. Vanderlinden’s work, which spans and often combines painting, collage, and drawing, resists assimilation into any single genre or style. title: 48 photographers selected from over 5200 for 167th Annual International Photography Exhibition
summary: The exhibiting artists for the 167th edition of the Royal Photographic Society’s International Photography Exhibition (IPE), the world’s longest-running photography exhibition, have been announced. Renowned for showcasing the diversity of contemporary photography from around the world, the works will be on display at London’s Saatchi Gallery from Friday 7th August to Friday 11th September 2026. More than 5200 photographers, both amateur and professional, submitted work for consideration in the 167th IPE open call. 113 prints from 48 photographers were selected by a guest panel for inclusion in the exhibition. title: Museo Jumex announces fall and winter 2026 exhibition lineup
summary: Museo Jumex’s fall and winter 2026 season underscores the scope and diversity of its curatorial program, reflecting the museum’s commitment to present both major surveys of internationally acclaimed artists and significant new projects by leading mid-career voices from Latin America and beyond. The season includes the first major survey of Richard Prince’s work in Latin America, an immersive installation produced for the museum by Álvaro Urbano, and Raúl Silva’s first solo exhibition in Mexico. The suite of exhibitions offers a broad perspective of contemporary art and will be on view from September 2026 through early February 2027. Richard Prince’s first major survey in Latin America, Tell Me Everything, opens September 26.
